brief:
Around 11,000 cancer patients in Gaza face critical conditions and imminent risk of death as essential medicines remain in severe shortage, the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights reported. The deficit encompasses chemotherapy drugs, lifesaving medications, and supportive treatments required for treatment protocols and symptom management.

The shortage has forced many patients to suspend their cancer treatment entirely, interrupting therapy regimens at crucial stages. Thousands of others have been deprived of access to necessary medicines altogether, leaving them without options for continued care. The crisis has created cascading health consequences across Gaza's most vulnerable population.
dek: Around 11,000 cancer patients in Gaza are suffering from critical conditions that put their lives at imminent risk amid an unprecedented and severe shortage of medicines essential for cancer treatment, including chemotherapy drugs, lifesaving medicines, and supportive treatments. This shortage has forced many patients to suspend their treatment protocols and has deprived thousands of others.
title: Cancer drug shortage in Gaza threatens 11,000 patients' lives.
